items.title: Bank 表示《GTA 6 Online》可能会在 2027 年初发布
items.summary: Take-Two's biggest release ever, GTA 6 , is coming up in November, but the company's share price continues to

content.v: Take-Two's biggest release ever, GTA 6 , is coming up in November, but the company's share price continues to drop. It's down 21% this year and has now dipped under $200 this week after reaching a 52-week high of $265.

In short, the stock is struggling , but one big bank says it sees a lot of upside, in part because Rockstar is expected to release a new version of GTA Online--potentially in the first quarter of 2027--that could generate loads of money.

"We recommend being long $TTWO through the GTA 6 launch," the bank said in a memo to investors seen by Business Insider . Being "long" means the investor would buy and hold. The bank said Take-Two stock "remains cheap."

In particular, Bank of America said investors are not fully appreciating how big GTA Online 2.0 could be. To be sure, Rockstar is calling GTA 6 a single-player game, but everyone expects multiplayer to arrive in some form eventually . GTA Online for GTA 5 has been, and continues to be, a huge moneymaker for Rockstar and Take-Two thanks to its many microtransactions. Many expect a new version of GTA Online for GTA 6 to up the ante even further and give players more reasons to spend time--and money--in the game.

Bank of America said a new version of GTA Online for GTA 6 could launch in the first calendar quarter of 2027, meaning January-March. This is also around the time that a PC edition of GTA 6 could arrive , driving even more revenue.
For comparison, both GTA 5 and Red Dead Redemption II launched without online multiplayer support, so it would not be shocking if GTA 6 followed the same playbook.

Bank of America has given Take-Two a "buy" rating and a price target of $330. That's below the company's previous $380 target, but still represents an upside of more than 60% based on the current stock price.
GTA 6 launches on November 19 for PS5 and Xbox Series X|S. The game's file size was recently revealed, and it's absolutely massive .

items.title: 《异形：隔离 2》团队确认实体版、照片模式和新游戏细节
items.summary: The team behind Alien: Isolation 2 released a Q&A that reveals new gameplay details, including using your real

content.v: https://assets-prd.ignimgs.com/2026/06/09/alien-isolation-2-preview-blogroll-1781007414832.jpg
The team behind Alien: Isolation 2 released a Q&A that reveals new gameplay details, including using your real-life microphone, a physical edition, a photo mode, and more.

The team at Creative Assembly released a 17-minute video outlining its vision for Alien: Isolation 2 by answering fan questions about the game, and there's a lot to look forward to. For starters, players can expect a physical edition of the game when it launches in 2027. That means it will beat the deadline to be published on a disc, just ahead of PlayStation's all-digital shift in 2028. The game will also boast a photo mode, which aims to be "everything you expect from a camera."

They're working hard to feature all of the detailed settings you'd expect from an actual camera, such as depth of field, lighting options, filters that call back to the original films, and more. As for the team building this game, about a third of the original crew that made the first title are working on the sequel, but they were looking for big fans when interviewing staff for the initial game. Lead game designer James Green called the sequel a "dream project."

Alien: Isolation 2 will be set months after the first game and, as revealed in a trailer , it will take place partially outside, which will allow the Xenomorph to behave differently. It will use the wider environment to hunt you more effectively by taking advantage of the rough weather and lack of claustrophobic environments where you can typically hear or see it coming. The team is once again trying to tap into the feeling of the original film, where a singular Xenomorph is hunting you as opposed to a whole army of them.

One big feature the team is also pushing is that you can enable an option to toggle your microphone on and off. This will take whatever audio is being fed into your mic, whether it be you screaming, setting down a cup on your desk, or your dog barking, and feed it back into the game. As a result, whatever noise you make in real life could theoretically attract the Xenomorph or other threats.

items.title: 《LOTRO》最新资料片现已推出，距游戏推出近 20 年
items.summary: The Lord of the Rings Online, an MMO based on the popular fantasy series, got its latest expansion today, some

content.v: The Lord of the Rings Online, an MMO based on the popular fantasy series, got its latest expansion today, some 19.5 years after the game was originally released in 2007.
The new expansion is called The Wolves of Mordor, and as its name suggests, the expansion is focused on the werewolves of Mordor who are going after the people who took down their master, Sauron.

The expansion takes players beyond Gorgoroth where they will "gather unlikely allies and uncover the secrets hidden in Mordor's forgotten corners." Players will visit three new regions: Heledhris, Parth Rhavas, and Nan Ogol. In those places, players can learn new skills and receive enhancements, and then mix and match them to create a unique playstyle.

The Wolves of Mordor expansion also adds new companions called Neighbors, who have their own unique personality traits and a "dynamic mood system." Players can forge friendships with these companions, and the companions can tell the player stories, provide gifts, and send them on missions.

The Wolves of Mordor is available in a $40 standard edition, an $80 Collector's Edition with extra cosmetics, and the $130 Ultimate Fan Bundle. This version comes with even more cosmetics, additional neighbor characters, and XP boosts, among other things.

The Lord of the Rings Online has added more than a dozen expansions since it was first released in 2007. The developer Turbine created the game, which began as a subscription-based MMO before pivoting to free-to-play in 2010. Warner Bros. originally published the game, but it changed hands to Daybreak Game Company, with development shifting to Standing Stone Games.

The Lord of the Rings Online has been up and running for nearly 20 years, but it's not the longest-running MMO out there. Blizzard's World of Warcraft launched in 2004 and has been running ever since, and has remained subscription-based the whole time. 1997's Ultima Online is also still up and running.

The wider Lord of the Rings universe remains in the zeitgeist, as Prime Video's The Rings of Power show comes back for its third season in November. After that, Andy Serkis is directing and starring in the 2027 movie The Hunt for Gollum.
There are more Lord of the Rings games in the works as well, including a "deeply immersive" game from Kingdom Come studio Warhorse.

items.title: 《Witchbrook》再次推迟，目前定于 2027 年上映
items.summary: We finally have a solid launch date, and it's not in 2026 as planned but it's not too far off, either.

content.v: One year after the cozy witch-life sim Witchbrook was delayed from 2025 to 2026, it's happened again, as the game is now slated to come out in 2027.
The good news is that unlike that previous delay , this one comes with a solid release date, and it's not too far off: The game is now slated to come out on January 28, 2027.

"We have poured detail and care into every pixel, to create a truly handcrafted experience. We can’t wait to open Witchbrook College’s grand doors to new students in January, and introduce you to the town and people of Mossport," developer Chucklefish and Robotality wrote in today's launch date announcement .

"Thank you for all of your support and patience, especially within the last year, while we took the additional time to make a game we’re truly proud of. We hope you’ll enjoy immersing yourself in our magical pixel art world as much as we’ve enjoyed making it."

It's been a long road for Witchbrook, which we first covered back in 2017, before it even had a title: Chucklefish merely teased it as "something like Stardew Valley meets Harry Potter ." In 2020, Chucklefish unveiled a dramatically overhauled visual style , and five years after that we finally got a release window , which didn't really work out. A year and a half after that, here we are, with fingers crossed that this new date—the first time Witchbrook has had a proper release date, to be clear—holds up.
Witchbrook will go for $25 on Steam , and Chucklefish is also working on physical editions, which will be revealed and released at some point after the initial launch.

items.title: 《博德之门 3》中最好的任务之一也是最可怕的，它与鬼魂或吸血鬼没有任何关系
items.summary: Drowning in consequences.

content.v: Baldur's Gate 3 has a lot of quests that feel resonant around this particularly spooky time of year. It has an elaborate haunted house that unravels a sordid saga of love and betrayal. It has vampires and vampire hunters. It has shadow monsters that hide in plain sight until you trigger an ambush. But none of these segments got my heart pumping as much as my trip down to the Iron Throne.
https://cdn.mos.cms.futurecdn.net/N5WXFQSCttV6Am7CopwTzd-1920-80.png
This article is brought to you by No More Room in Hell 2 .

Aesthetically, this return to our old pal Sarevok's sunken stomping grounds isn't nearly the creepiest or most unsettling part of the adventure. That would probably have to go to the Mindflayer Colony below Moonrise Towers. It's a murky prison full of evil fish men and some unpleasant surprises, but the somewhat BioShock-esque decor isn't doing the heavy lifting on its own. The key here is that it's one of the only places Baldur's Gate 3 flips our mechanical expectations on their head to create genuine panic and terror.
The reason I feel my stomach starting to churn every time I approach this quest on a new playthrough is that diabolical timer.

If you haven't been here before, I'll keep it light on story spoilers. But basically, the party has to rescue a group of captive gnomes and a couple important plot characters from an underwater prison run by the Sword Coast's own Prince of Cringe, Enver Gortash. He's not exactly thrilled by your submarine escapades, though, and triggers a series of events that will flood the prison and kill anyone in it after six frantic rounds.

If that doesn't sound like a lot of time, it really isn't—especially not if you're coming into this for the first time without knowing what's about to happen or how to prepare. Anyone who hasn't made it back to the sub when that timer expires dies horribly by either drowning or the sudden, crushing pressure of an ocean compressing them into slush.

And of course, this being Baldur's Gate 3, even the gnome civilians who aren't relevant to the story have names, relationships, and recorded dialogue if they survive. You aren't losing generic pawns here. You're failing well-written people.
https://cdn.mos.cms.futurecdn.net/Xfypc76vV9rNYPjU9JyKUE-1920-80.jpg

If you're not playing Honor Mode, party members who didn't make it out will have their lifeless bodies wash up on shore where they can be revived by Withers or whatever miraculous magic you might have access to. If you are, you can say goodbye to them forever. And everyone else who can possibly die during this sequence is simply dead as all get out. This can even include one very major NPC with a role to play in the story and a strong connection to one particular member of the party.
Can't save em all

In almost every other case, undoing a mistake or seeing a different path in Baldur's Gate 3 is a simple matter of reloading a save. And sure, you could reload back to the very beginning of the Iron Throne quest and try to do it better. But due to the structure of the quest, this isn't as simple as redoing a boss fight or picking a different dialogue option. This sprawling dungeon with locked cells, flooded corridors, and tough enemies is just grueling enough that the idea of trying again isn't particularly attractive. It's designed to make savescumming feel painful and daunting, encouraging you to live with the consequences of your actions.
By giving us a puzzle to solve using the turn-based action economy with lethal consequences for small errors, Larian created a deep well of fear beneath the sea.

On a first playthrough, and unprepared, you may find it's not even possible to save everyone. I've done it once, and it required hours of prep with haste spells, teleportation, portal scrolls, telekinesis—everything I could muster to give me any kind of advantage. You almost have to plan out every action for every character in advance. Even one mistake could mean you find yourself deciding who to leave behind.

As much as it made my heart pound and forced me to experience the cold sting of failure when I had to explain to one of my gnome allies that his loved one didn't make it, this was easily one of BG3's best quests. I'll never forget how it felt the first time through. And even as a very experienced player now, with hundreds of hours across multiple playthroughs, it never feels trivial. It never feels like something I can take for granted if I want everybody to survive.
By giving us a puzzle to solve using the turn-based action economy with lethal consequences for small errors, Larian created a deep well of fear beneath the sea.
https://cdn.mos.cms.futurecdn.net/pmDBr4e6BSJeHkm9woCcwE-1920-80.jpg
https://cdn.mos.cms.futurecdn.net/rsVgMYfCm3xYH7ppYHJdkE-1920-80.jpg
https://cdn.mos.cms.futurecdn.net/F5mg6W5dy7GTiiip4KRZME-1920-80.jpg
https://cdn.mos.cms.futurecdn.net/owjJ5zdvLEGzWV6HjzkmtE-1920-80.jpg
https://cdn.mos.cms.futurecdn.net/UCLLZ63nUUBWYTjjMhGXzE-1920-80.jpg

Though I try to limit my savescumming, I've never had the stomach to brave it out in Honor Mode, where the consequences of all of my mistakes would become permanent. Maybe if I did, I'd come to feel differently about the Iron Throne. At that point, would it just become another life-or-death adventure like any other? Would wandering around the Underdark creep me out just as much as boarding that submersible?
I would love to see more developers try to instill fear by subverting expectations about failure and consequences.

While that may be, the fact that the Iron Throne works the way it does means players like me get to experience a little taste of that permadeath anxiety. It's easy to be a hero when the F5 key is right there. It's a true champion who can soldier on when you only have one shot. And so, while it might be Baldur's Gate 3's scariest quest, I also found it to be one of the most gratifying. Even though I couldn't save everyone the first time through, that bittersweet victory felt hard-won and honest.

I would love to see more developers try to instill fear by subverting expectations about failure and consequences. It can be far more effective than a jump scare or an unkillable pursuer like you see in so many more traditional horror games. Especially in an era where run-based games are ascendant, and every defeat is nothing but a new beginning, I long to have the threat of living with a bad outcome held over me. Even if I do succeed, that thrill adds a lot to the experience.
I've stood here before, and it never fails to make my throat feel dry. The waves churn. The hatch opens. Those prisoners are down there counting on me.
Here we go again.

items.title: Valve 承认 Steam 存在人工智能溢出和克隆问题，但表示“我们不想成为告诉开发者应该或不应该使用哪些工具的看门人”
items.summary: Steam Next Fest is being flooded with thousands of low-effort games, while developers are becoming reluctant t

content.v: The rise of AI slop is a real problem for Steam. Developers are growing wary of sharing their concepts and demos for fear of them being cloned , while Next Fest events meant to showcase upcoming games are being choked by literally thousands of demos hastily cranked out by 'developers' who are throwing everything imaginable at the wall in hopes that something will stick.

Speaking at the Steam Indie Connect event in Busan, South Korea, Valve's Tom Giardino and Marc Wilkinson acknowledged the problem, which as reported by Inven Global included at least one instance of a developer reporting extortion threats: "If you don't pay, we'll clone your game with AI and release it first." But the pair suggested that Valve isn't really in a position to do much about it, at least as far as regulating what is and isn't allowed on the platform. "We don't want to be gatekeepers telling developers which tools they should or shouldn't use," Giardino said.

Noting that games were being cloned long before AI came on the scene—just at a much slower pace—Giardino suggested that developers can protect their work by first building a strong community around it, and then focusing on continual improvements: "Rather than relying on a single mechanic that someone can easily copy, you need to keep growing your game by adding features, personality, and creativity that stem from your own perspective."

Valve's approach to the deluge of AI games flooding the Steam Next Fest is similar. Wilkinson said that during the first two days of the event, Steam users are shown games virtually randomly—but after that, the platform starts making personalized recommendations, showing users games they're more likely to enjoy. The goal of that early randomization, he explained, is to give every developer a fair shot at visibility, before drilling down into actual preferences.

"We recognize that the trade-off is some low-quality games get exposed," Wilkinson said. "We are fully aware of the situation, and a significant number of people are thinking about how to solve this problem."
It is a problem—this SteamDB chart of Steam game releases by year very clearly illustrates why:
https://cdn.mos.cms.futurecdn.net/HQPjqNoEXSnJ7VTaCN4Xd3-1920-80.png

Nearly 23,000 games have been released on Steam in 2026 alone, and it's not even November yet. Most of them are garbo, irrespective of the role AI played in their development, but it's still an incredible mass of videogames that users and developers alike have to wrestle with. It may not be an issue for major studios releasing big name games, but for the person plugging away on what might potentially be the next Animal Well, Balatro, or Vampire Survivors, the risk of being swept away in a flood of low-effort slop and clones is inescapable.

Israel Mallén of Digital Suns Games, which cancelled a planned Moonlighter demo on Steam over worries that it would be cloned, recently suggested that storefronts like Steam could help combat unethical game cloning by giving developers "more tools to vet who gets access [to pre-release builds], like account age, playtime or review history."

But while Valve is grappling with the problem, it doesn't sound like major changes of that sort are imminent: Giardino acknowledged that "there's plenty of room for improvement" but said, "Rather than limiting developer access, making Steam a smarter and more dynamic platform is the starting point of our philosophy."

items.title: Backrooms 导演凯恩·帕森斯 (Kane Parsons) 目前正穿着 Valve 连帽衫从事“3 个梦想项目”——可疑
items.summary: I'm calling it now—Half-Life 3 will be a patchwork of YouTube shorts.

content.v: Fans of horror or obscure liminal spaces have been eating exceptionally well this year, what with all the outstanding horror games and movies—one of which being Kane Parsons' silver screen debut, The Backrooms film. As a fan of Parsons' YouTube series I was pretty confident that this film would nail the Backrooms, and I was right . But now that's done, fans are left wondering what's next for Parsons.

There have been rumours of a Backrooms sequel swirling pretty much since the first screening of the film ended, but there's nothing concrete. Parsons, though, has since confirmed during an interview with The Kyle Buchanan Show that he's working "on three dream projects, currently". So if we assume The Backrooms sequel is one of them, what could the other two be? Well, it could have something to do with the Valve hoodie Parsons is wearing in the interview.
https://cdn.mos.cms.futurecdn.net/PR2EZjW3BitwkW5ttpmo9k-1920-80.jpg

Parsons has shared stories about going to visit Valve HQ on his social media a couple of times, each one sparking new rumours of the potential collaboration that he could be cooking up. He's openly talked about how influential the Portal games have been on his creative journey, so most fans are betting on that as his adaptation of choice. But mum's the word: "They'd get me with their space lasers if I speak about it," Parsons says. "They can see through walls. They're very serious." Yup, sounds like Valve to me.

The most Parsons can talk about when it comes to Valve is just how nice they are. "They're lovely people over there," Parsons adds. "They work in experiments, and I like that because that tends to be how I work. I don't really have a desire to sensationalise anything I may or may not be talking to them about over there." He goes on to explain how there's not a whole lot to report back on: if anything is going on it's in the super early stages—mostly just figuring out whether there's something there and, if so, does it align with both creative visions.

"It's more like having an abstract creative conversation that could flow in 30 different directions," Parsons says. "If you just know the way Valve works I think they're looking to experiment internally more than anything that can be talked about. If something cool comes of it I'm sure somehow people will know."

For the most part it just seems like Parsons is trying to keep his options open and make deliberate moves that'll help his skills grow: "I'm trying to make sure that I'm not rushing into [things], I'm trying not to bite off more than I can chew. And I'm trying to pick things that will force me to learn about subjects that I think are foundational."

items.title: WoW: Forever Content Updates Will Come Slower Than You Might Expect
items.summary: Developer Blizzard's new version of its flagship MMORPG, World of Warcraft: Forever , will receive content upd

content.v: Developer Blizzard's new version of its flagship MMORPG, World of Warcraft: Forever , will receive content updates "every four months," avoiding modern WoW's somewhat controversial eight-week patch cycle.

In an interview with IGN , Forever principal game designer Kris Zierhut revealed the content schedule plan and explained Blizzard's reasoning. He said WoW Classic's Season of Discovery received updates "way too fast," every 8-10 weeks.

Since the launch of WoW's Dragonflight expansion in 2022, an eight-week update schedule is also what modern WoW operates on. Its more frequent patch schedule means there's always something new to do, but has been criticized by some players due to the buggy nature of recent updates and lackluster content.

On the other hand, some older expansions, like Warlords of Draenor and Shadowlands, saw content droughts that lasted six months or more, leaving players hungry for something new to do. Forever will split the difference.
"We're fairly convinced the correct [update] rate is something closer to once every four months or 17 weeks or three times a year," Zierhut said.

Just because major updates will be coming every four or so months doesn't mean there won't be anything new to do between patches. Zierhut said some content will unlock partway through those four-month patch cycles.

"It's not just patch day comes [around], here's a content fire hose, and now we're silent for four months," he said. "A lot of that is, 'Hey, there's a time event calendar that gradually unlocks things and opens them up over those four months' to give things a little bit more life instead of all at once."

According to a Forever content roadmap released during BlizzCon 2026, the latest version of Blizzard's MMORPG will receive its first major update in Spring 2027. That update will add new raids, dungeons, and quests, and mark the start of a new PvP season. Another major update is slated for Summer 2027 and will add yet another new raid, revamp an existing raid from WoW Classic, add two additional dungeons, see a new legendary item and quest chain, and introduce updates to the game's professions and its new Legacy system.

WoW: Forever launches on November 4, but you can technically go ahead and make your character now if you paid for the game's new playable race. With less than a week before launch, Blizzard has been busy announcing changes and improvements ahead of its release, with major changes to racial abilities , improvements to layering , and the addition of a new server option .

items.title: 《沉睡的狗》电影导演解释了为什么改编花了这么长时间
items.summary: Like many video game movies , Sleeping Dogs seems stuck in development hell. Even though it looked like progre

content.v: Like many video game movies , Sleeping Dogs seems stuck in development hell. Even though it looked like progress on this adaptation of the cult-classic action game was once again picking up when Shang-Chi star Simu Liu started teasing new developments last year, and Timo Tjahjanto (Nobody 2) was later announced as the director , there's been little word since on whether the film will ever get off the ground. What's taking so long? According to Tjahjanto, the slow approach is by design.

"Trust me when I say Simu and I are doing our best to slowly make this come into fruition," Tjahjanto wrote on X/Twitter . "Trying to stay as loyal to Wei Shen's tale while adding layers to make the narrative more fitting into a feature film is not an easy task. We're taking our time to make the best version of [Sleeping Dogs] the movie."
https://www.gamespot.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/05/Sleeping-Dogs-1.jpg?w=636

Sleeping Dogs isn't exactly a complex story, as the 2012 game saw undercover cop Wei Shen's loyalties tested after he infiltrated a Hong Kong triad and found himself in the middle of a gangland civil war. It's a fairly standard tale for a game inspired by Hong Kong action movies, unless Tjahjanto is trying to weave in the DLC's story, which introduced an undead army and magical tea.

Sleeping Dogs is hardly the first video game adaptation to simmer in the background, as dozens of other projects are currently in varying stages of development. One notable example is the Ghost of Tsushima movie, which Chad Stahelski has been attached to direct for several years now; last we heard, Stahelski said a script was ready .

That was in 2023, and with the John Wick director currently working on finishing up the new Highlander movie starring Henry Cavill, don't expect to see Jin Sakai in the live-action flesh anytime soon--at least an anime adaptation of the popular samurai open-world game will land in 2028.

items.title: 《Arc Raiders》的执行制作人对添加 PvE 持“有点怀疑”，但在成功测试之后，团队需要决定“我们接下来要做什么”
items.summary: I say just replicate the PvE test for those who want it.

content.v: I enjoyed having the palate cleanser that was Arc Raiders limited-time PvE test for the short week it was here. It provided a chill alternative to the usual chaos and cheater-laden PvP, where I could fight some tough arcs, enjoy the map, and interact with players without the fear of getting ratted. And clearly I'm not the only one who enjoyed it, as Embark confirmed over 30 million PvE sessions were played during the test period.

But running the test was only half the battle, now Embark needs to decide whether it's worth adding a dedicated PvE mode to the game. Previously, the team has confirmed that it'll need some extra time to get its ducks in order ahead of making any concrete decisions, but now executive producer Aleksander Grøndal has given us a little bit more information concerning the decision process.
https://cdn.mos.cms.futurecdn.net/kbb383K662vHCMhKMQQjUM-1920-80.jpg

"Now that we’ve concluded the PvE matchmaking toggle test, we’re doing a deep dive into what that means," Grøndal says in an interview with MP1st . "Of course, we were a bit skeptical about bringing such a mode to the game for historical reasons, but now we need to discuss what we want to do going forward."

The idea of adding PvE to Arc Raiders has been slightly controversial, with some players arguing it misses the point of the game, may inflate the junk economy, or even take players away from PvP. I certainly don't think PvE should replace PvP, but that was never an option; I do believe, however, as with accessibility options, that giving players more choice is rarely a bad thing.

The PvE test also attempted to solve the issue of loot inflation by offering worse scrap in PvE lobbies. You also can't get the newest high end loot either , so I doubt it'll be a game-breaking issue. The bigger issue in my eyes is interest in Arc Raiders waning again, something that a PvE mode, among other things, could fix.
https://cdn.mos.cms.futurecdn.net/adiLjp7UMA8xcLqb82xVtc-1920-80.jpg

"I think the game has an appeal in its nature and that a certain player type wants to play the game without the stress, you know," Grøndal explains. "Perhaps this is more a signal that the game could support more player types, and we need to figure out how to support that. The challenge, of course, is how we do that without undermining the premise of the game itself.

"That is exactly what we need to consider now, but before we get to the content discussion, we need to understand what the need is here. Is it more a chill side mode you can play between more intense PvPvE rounds? Is it more a challenge mode that you can test your skills against AI? Or perhaps it’s a full experience with PvE only? These are some of the questions we need to dig into before we decide how to go forward. All options will have different implications on how we build future game updates."

Adding a permanent PvE mode certainly won't be easy. It'll mean more nuanced balancing and future updates will have to take PvPvE and PvE into account. While I'd certainly like to see it happen I wouldn't hold it against Embark for not wanting to take extra work on, especially since the devs have been so open about combatting crunch and how much work a live service game like Arc Raiders takes to maintain .

items.title: 如果你喜欢恐怖但又讨厌被吓到，我为你准备了完美的万圣节游戏
items.summary: It's unsettling and occasionally startling, but still immensely sweet.

content.v: https://cdn.mos.cms.futurecdn.net/N5WXFQSCttV6Am7CopwTzd-1920-80.png
This article is brought to you by No More Room in Hell 2 .

I used to enjoy horror movies and games a lot, but as I get older I find I'm not that interested in being scared out of my wits. I love all the trappings of horror: the tension, the atmosphere, the monsters. But the actual scary stuff? I'd rather pass, honestly.

That's one of many reasons that Creature Kitchen is the perfect game for me to play this Halloween week. It's spooky, it's unsettling, it's occasionally startling, but it's not really scary at all. It's actually downright sweet, the perfect treat for any fellow scaredy cats this Halloween.

In Creature Kitchen you find yourself in the darkened woods late at night, drawn to a small, creaky cabin by a mysterious light. Once there you can begin poking around: opening drawers, peering into the fridge, frowning at locked doors and jumping at the occasional clap of thunder and flash of lightning. In nearly any other game you'd soon be fighting for your life, but here, you've got a different mission: start cooking.

The woods and house are filled with creatures. Some aren't too surprising: a mouse living in the walls, for example. Others fall into the cryptid category and are more alarming, at least at first. Your job is to take an old camera and photograph these entities, which adds an entry into your diary. Once you've taken a picture of a creepy creature, your diary will give you some hints about what it might like to eat.
https://cdn.mos.cms.futurecdn.net/8RCbBZb2BDap3Dxhwrp78Q-1920-80.jpg

Then you hunt for recipes and ingredients: some in the weird pantry that seems infinitely deep, some hidden in the drawers and among the knickknacks in the cabin, and some in the yard and shadowy woods beyond the fence. Prepare your ingredients in a frying pan, mixing bowl, or chopping board, then put them in a paper bag and feed them to the correct beastie.

These hungry creatures may look like monsters, but they're just your neighbors, really, and there's no better way to make a new friend than over a tasty meal. Serve these cuddly cryptids the foods they like and they'll give you a key that unlocks something new in your cabin leading to new ingredients, recipes, and secrets.
https://cdn.mos.cms.futurecdn.net/fAo4i2387nZh7NV3YWd9BQ-1920-80.jpg

The cooking system is great, there are some clever puzzles hidden around, and the cryptids, while initially unnerving to be around, eventually feel like your cuddly besties. There's one, I admit, that startled me a bit just about every time I saw it lurching around outside, but then something happened. The times I went out and didn't see it I'd get worried. Is it OK? Is it coming back? Do I actually… miss that giant weirdo?

Creature Kitchen is a real joy. It's spooky yet sweet, with a genuinely unsettling horror atmosphere that somehow fits perfectly with its wholesome message. It's one of my favorite games of the year, and if you really enjoy horror but hate actually being scared, I think you should grab it on Steam and get cooking.

items.title: 吸血鬼是一款黑暗、残酷的大型多人在线角色扮演游戏，专注于血腥暴力
items.titleEn: Vampir Is a Dark, Brutal MMORPG Focused on Bloody Violence

content.v: https://assets-prd.ignimgs.com/2026/10/21/vampir-game-overview-01-keyart-1792619336828.jpg
MMORPG 类型一直严重缺乏吸血鬼形象，但 Netmarble 的《吸血鬼》却填补了这一空缺。它于 2025 年首次在韩国推出，最近扩展到西方，现在可以在美国的 PC、iOS 和 Android 平台上使用。
这是一款真正倾向于完整吸血鬼体验的游戏。它的定义是血腥、恐怖和性，以及黑暗奇幻背景中的残酷战斗。从游戏一开始，你就会看到一些可怕的场景，这些场景奠定了世界的基调，而这种基调也会融入到游戏玩法中。有五个角色类别可供选择，他们都是侵略性的伤害制造者，可以使用吸血鬼标志性的吸血能力来恢复生命值并获得暂时的战斗增益。
https://assets-prd.ignimgs.com/2026/10/21/vampir-game-overview-03-1792619545063.png
所有课程都以时尚的方式呈现死亡，但他们的方式却截然不同。 Carnage可以使用多种枪械进行速射攻击。血污是一名具有额外耐用性的狂战士，可以将其嗜血转化为一把强大的剑。毒蛇使用毒药、诅咒和召唤生物来造成范围伤害并控制战场。死神是一名隐形刺客，使用传送和镰刀来造成致命一击。而阿卡莎是一个专门追击敌人的近战职业。

No matter which class you’re playing, you’ll feel the impact of your attacks. Battles are marked by dismemberment that leaves bloodstains in their wake. High-quality graphics add to the impact, with a level of fidelity that’s particularly impressive on mobile. The dark vibe and aesthetics are heightened by the use of lighting and shadows, and character models are detailed with nicely rendered skin textures.
https://assets-prd.ignimgs.com/2026/10/21/vampir-game-overview-07-1792619596571.jpg

Since different people play MMOs for different reasons, Vampir provides separate spaces for people who want to focus on progression or competition. If you prefer to level up your character and gather resources with relative ease, you can do that on individual servers with no issue. If you’re the competitive type, you can jump into Gehenna, an inter-server PvP battlefield that becomes available early in the game.

Gehenna is a dedicated combat zone that can pit you against players with server honor on the line. You can form clans to team up with other players and compete together. Bosses will appear at set times, and defeating them can earn rewards for you and honor for your server, as well as high-value rewards delivered to your Clan Vault. It’s also possible to physically block the routes of other players during these boss battles, allowing your clan to form battle lines and giving you strategic options to ensure victory.

Gehenna content is split into seasons, with server matchups reshuffled when each new season begins. This creates new rivalries and prevents a single clan from monopolizing competition for an extended period of time.
还有合作挑战，比如防御模式，你需要共同努力，保卫你的氏族徽章免受一波又一波的攻击。竞技内容涵盖从小规模冲突到大规模战斗，包括季节性氏族占领战争和官方锦标赛。在这些大型比赛中脱颖而出的部落将获得游戏所能提供的最高奖励。
除了这些奖励之外，您还可以通过游戏内商店获得角色升级资源。您可以用钻石购买这些钻石，您可以通过野外游戏赚取钻石，而无需花钱，最高可达每周耕作限额。钻石还用于吸血鬼扭蛋系统中的召唤，这为该类型的标准怜悯系统添加了独特的机制。
https://assets-prd.ignimgs.com/2026/10/21/vampir-game-overview-09-1792619617101.jpg
对于每个非传奇级的召唤，您都会获得护理点，并在达到一定的点阈值时获得奖励。较低等级的召唤结果会奖励更多的护理点，因此普通奖励比罕见奖励更多，而罕见奖励比稀有奖励更多。因此，如果你得到一串普通召唤，它实际上会加速你迈向传奇拉力的进程。
《吸血鬼》现已登陆PC、iOS、Android平台，并推出特别上线奖励活动，只要开始游戏即可获得指定英雄坐骑召唤券、一亿金币以及全套稀有装备。通过游戏，你还可以获得英雄装备和1,100次召唤机会。要了解最新更新，您可以关注游戏 YouTube、Facebook 和 Discord。

items.title: 任天堂的独立世界演示对于一个简短的节目来说非常拥挤
items.summary: The latest Indie World Showcase only lasted for a bit longer than 15 minutes, but that small time window didn'

content.v: The latest Indie World Showcase only lasted for a bit longer than 15 minutes, but that small time window didn't stop Nintendo from featuring some truly cool-looking games. The Witchbrook release date announcement kicked things off for the presentation. While definitely exciting, that's not what enthralled me the most.

That's because the next unveiling was Winds of Viridia, an action-adventure game from developer Shark Jump that appears inspired by The Legend of Zelda: Breath of the Wild. You play as a brown-haired boy who teams up with an adorable mothbug. But the cute companion is also apparently lethal against foes. Other things we're digging about this single-player title is how much the protagonist does stylistic spin moves as well as Hollow Knight: Silksong composer Christopher Larkin's involvement with the music. Plus, there's a demo available now on Switch 2, with a full release expected for early next year.

City of None followed up Winds of Viridia and kept our eyes glued to the screen. The retro pixel art is stunning, and this is coming from someone who feels burnt out by a lot of the throwback aesthetics these days. Maybe the changing four-color palette is what ultimately does it for me. Anyway, the action-puzzle platformer comes from Celeste co-creator Noel Berry--along with his brother, Liam. Celeste is one of my favorite 2D games of the past 10 years, so that connection alone has me standing up. City of None is coming to Switch and Switch 2 in 2027.

The next title worth mentioning gives Square Enix a run for its money in the HD-2D space: Threads of Time. The JRPG from Balor Games and Riyo Games seems heavily influenced by Chrono Trigger, with players traveling to the Middle Ages and even a cyberpunk future. The turn-based battling looks classic yet captivating, and we'll see if the story can match the grandiose nature of the setup. It's aiming for a Summer 2027 launch on Switch and Switch 2.

Obviously, these three games were just a sample from the Indie World Showcase, but they really stood out. A few other things we noticed from the show were multiple titles featuring raccoons, oddly; a popular golf game on Steam coming to Switch 2; and a roguelike brawler from a Dead Cells developer called Tenjutsu.
